The caller-supplied url may be absolute or relative and may contain a Location header whose value is untrusted: it can be absolute, contain .. segments, use JavaScript protocol, or be out of range. The dangerous operation is opening and reading an HTTP response on the provided url. Raise ValueError if the scheme is not http or https and raise ValueError if the requested port is not the default port for the scheme (80 for http, 443 for https). Resolve the url's hostname to its textual IP address(es) using resolve_host(hostname) and raise ValueError unless exactly one IP address is returned. Follow at most five HTTP redirects, resolving each Location header against the current URL and raising ValueError if the resolved Location does not share the same scheme, port, and credentials as the initial destination, raise ValueError if the resolved Location's DNS cannot be resolved to a single IP address, and raise ValueError if the resolved Location is out of range. Check the status code of the final response and raise ValueError unless it is exactly 200, then return the response body as text.
END_PLAN
